notes: NEEDS VERIFICATION (re-checked 2026-10-05): still no Cypriot primary source for ordinary (non-controlled) prescription medicines carried by travellers. The Pharmaceutical Services 'Narcotics and Psychotropics' page covers only internationally controlled medicines (permits for visitors; already published as controlled-medication-cy); its linked 'Guidelines for Travellers Carrying Personal Medication' PDF is a generic 2003 UN guideline, not Cyprus rules; the Pharmaceutical Services FAQ (dmlfaq_gr) returned HTTP 500. Secondary sites claim a 3-month supply is fine without prescription — unconfirmed, do not use. notes: NEEDS VERIFICATION (re-checked 2026-10-05). Confirmed on primary sources: Cyprus Customs' passenger allowances list tobacco products and alcohol only — e-cigarettes and e-liquid are not among them (Channel system and concessions page, last updated 5/2/2020); e-liquid, with or without nicotine, is a nationally excisable product at €0.12 per ml (Excise Duties — General Information, Excise Duty Law 91(I)/2004 Part XII); cross-border distance sales of e-cigarettes and refill containers to consumers are prohibited (Health Protection (Smoking Control) Regulations 2017, arts 20 and 22(8)). Not confirmed: whether a traveller's personal e-liquid is relieved under the general €430 'other goods' allowance or owes the excise duty — no primary source states this, so no verdict is published.
